body.estimand_functional:
Unconditionally on the exact-uniform class,
\[
R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}
\gtrsim R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F.
\]
For the common-support and common-constant slice of Kennedy et al.'s Theorem~1 lower-bound class,
\[
R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP},K}
\gtrsim
\left\{n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)}\vee
n^{-2/(2+d/\gamma+d/q)}\right\}
\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F.
\]
Only conditional on an affirmative resolution of the full-fiber occupancy lift does the exact-uniform relation strengthen to
\[
R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}
\asymp R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F.
\]
No adaptive risk relation or logarithmic adaptation penalty is asserted.

sampling_model.units: The observed records \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary observational treatment with unknown Hölder propensity \(\pi\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The proposed target-fiber mechanism profiles over the full propensity and control-regression Hölder classes; no named nuisance estimator and no fixed finite nuisance sieve is assumed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem~1 gives the nonprivate pointwise Hölder-CATE lower bound on a class whose covariate density is bounded above; Theorem~2 treats attainability under separate estimator and design conditions.
Section~4 uses treated--control occupancy and effect homogeneity to obtain a global nonprivate rate with a collision term.
The paper stabilizes central-private U-statistics using local Hájek projections and tuple reweighting.
Section~4 gives a general pure-private T-mechanism based on clipped likelihood-ratio tests and finite covers.
The paper gives central-private Le Cam, Fano, and Assouad inequalities based on expected Hamming transport.
Theorems~1 and~3 give finite-query and functional observational CATE releases under approximate differential privacy.

The paper analyzes sample-split differentially private CATE meta-learners and privacy--utility guarantees, but does not establish a pure-central-DP pointwise Hölder minimax converse or an occupancy frontier.
The sparse-histogram lower bound and compact dense-histogram theorem show that pure-private costs can change with representation and occupancy.
Their multiscale and adaptive-lower-bound arguments are templates for the separate unresolved adaptation question; no adaptive rate or logarithmic penalty is imported here.
The paper establishes nonprivate heterogeneous-effect minimax rates with explicit random-design geometry.
Definition~2 and Section~4 construct T-estimators from coherent tests on countable model nets.

body.tldr: The occupancy-weighted score has an unconditional exact expectation and constant replacement sensitivity, while the exact-uniform Hölder class has unconditional \(\rho_G\) and \(\rho_F\) pure-private lower-bound terms in addition to its nonprivate minimax floor.  Inclusion in the common-support and common-constant slice of Kennedy et al.'s Theorem~1 lower-bound class transfers all of these converse terms upward.  The full-fiber occupancy lift remains the unresolved upper-construction crux on the exact-uniform class, so a matching upper frontier is only conditional; adaptation is downstream and wholly open, with no adaptive rate or logarithmic penalty claimed.

project_justification.gap: No located result gives a pure-central-DP minimax frontier for pointwise CATE with unknown smooth propensity and outcome regression. The closest banked construction uses only exactly-two-record cells and therefore loses all signal when cell occupancy diverges.
project_justification.niche: Realized cell occupancy can amplify a degenerate nuisance-product signal while preserving constant record influence, potentially joining the sparse \(n^2\epsilon\) branch to the dense \(n\epsilon\) branch with no third radius.
project_justification.fill: The project proves exact expectation and constant-sensitivity identities for the weighted pair score and the \(\rho_F\) and \(\rho_G\) pure-private lower-bound terms unconditionally on the exact-uniform class, then transfers that converse upward to the common-support and common-constant slice of Kennedy et al.'s Theorem~1 bounded-above-density lower-bound class.  The exact-uniform matching upper bound is only a conditional reduction from the unresolved full-fiber weighted-shell certificate, and the downstream adaptation problem remains wholly open with no claimed rate or logarithmic penalty.

body.related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman's Theorem~1 gives the nonprivate pointwise Hölder-CATE lower bound on a class requiring the covariate density only to be bounded above.  Their Theorem~2 addresses attainability under separate estimator and design conditions, including additional local-support requirements; the two theorems are not treated here as defining one class.  The present exact-uniform class is a subclass of the common-support and common-constant Theorem~1 slice: the causal constructions prove the \(\rho_G\) and \(\rho_F\) privacy lower-bound terms on that subclass, and minimax monotonicity transfers every lower-bound term upward.  No upper bound is transferred.  Niu, Nori, Quistorff, Caruana, Ngwe, and Kannan analyze sample-split differentially private CATE meta-learners and their privacy--utility guarantees, but do not give a pure-central-DP pointwise Hölder minimax converse or an occupancy frontier.  Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy motivate conditioning on realized occupancy; Chaudhuri, Loh, Pandey, and Sarkar motivate stable local projections; and Acharya, Sun, and Zhang supply the private Hamming-coupling inequality used in the converse.  Birgé and Asi, Duchi, Haque, Li, and Ruan provide test-selection templates for the unresolved exact-uniform full-fiber construction.  Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel study approximate-private CATE releases rather than this pure-private minimax problem.  Balcer and Vadhan illustrate occupancy-dependent privacy transitions.  Cai, Chakraborty, and Vuursteen provide templates only for a separate downstream open adaptation question: this note claims neither an adaptive rate nor a logarithmic adaptation penalty.  Gao and Han analyze distinct nonprivate random-design geometry.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The identity in Lemma 2 does not itself solve the full-fiber problem. For arbitrary least-favorable priors, the second-order kernel orientation can depend on a growing nuisance profile, and clipping local projections can reintroduce a sieve-size factor. The proposed early kill test is the finite \(d=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/8\), \(\gamma=1\) two-resolution program from the parent archive: impose every replacement-neighbor constraint, increase both occupancy and nuisance-sign dimension, and reject the route if the optimized weighted-shell functional grows with the nuisance dimension after occupancy weighting.
body.honest_scope: The unconditional results are the occupancy identity, the nonprivate floor, and the \(\rho_G\) and \(\rho_F\) pure-private lower-bound terms on the fixed-smoothness exact-uniform class, together with their upward lower-bound transfer to the common-support and common-constant slice of Kennedy et al.'s Theorem~1 class, whose design density is bounded above but need not be bounded below.  No superclass upper bound is asserted.  On the exact-uniform class, the full-fiber occupancy lift is the unresolved upper-construction crux, and the matching frontier theorem is only a conditional reduction from that premise.  Smoothness adaptation is downstream and wholly open; no adaptive rate or logarithmic penalty is claimed.
